text: Start: mobile testing harness + guide. Reading todo card, mobile-pinch-zoom test, and researching iOS-from-Windows debugging.

iOS research done. Safari Web Inspector needs macOS, but ios-webkit-debug-proxy + ios-safari-remote-debug-kit works from Windows for free via the Apple Devices app; inspect.dev is the paid one at 79 USD/yr, free tier 15 min/day. Key fact: when iOS kills the WebContent process no onerror fires, so the only signal is a breadcrumb written before the crash. Building the harness around that.

Harness built and green: scripts/mobile-diag-server.mjs + tools/mobile-diag.js, 6 cases pass under Pixel 5 emulation with real CDP pinches. Two mutation runs confirm the test can fail. Machine check: no inbound firewall rule exists for node on any profile and the wifi is categorised Public, so a phone on wifi cannot reach this machine today. Android over USB with adb reverse sidesteps that entirely. iTunes and Apple Mobile Device Support are already installed, which is the hard prerequisite for the iOS route.
